title: Genomics
description: Four letters, three billion of them. Unlocks the Gene Sequencer, recombinant DNA and engineered enzymes.

puzzle.goal: A genome of length G is shredded into N random reads of length L, each placed independently at a uniformly random position. A given base is covered by a read with probability L/G. Write the probability that a given base is covered by exactly k reads.
puzzle.name: Lander–Waterman coverage statistics
puzzle.form: binom ( N , k ) * ( L / G ) ^ k * ( 1 - L / G ) ^ ( N - k )
puzzle.ask: For many reads this becomes a Poisson distribution of mean C = LN/G, so P₀ = e^(−C). Find the fraction of the genome covered at least once for L = @{L} bp, N = @{N} million reads and G = 3000 Mbp (L·N/G = @{L} × @{N} / 3000).

vars.k: number of reads covering the base

puzzle.method: Each read is an independent trial that covers the base or not: count the ways to choose which k of the N reads cover it.
